pack.title: Signaling Basics (Example)
pack.description: Illustrative example pack: basic emergency signaling practice. Educational sample content for the ODY format.

sources.title: General public emergency signaling guidance (illustrative example)

entries.title: Distress signals
entries.summary: Use repeated, clearly distinguishable signals to indicate that you need help.
entries.detail: Three of anything is a widely recognized distress pattern: three whistle blasts, three fires, three light flashes. Space repetitions so they are clearly deliberate.
actions: Use a repeating pattern of three
checklist: The pattern is repeated and deliberate
decision_rules: If a signal is answered, stop and listen for instructions
If there is no answer, rest and repeat at intervals
prohibitions: Do not signal continuously without pauses
Do not leave your position to chase a response

entries.title: Making yourself visible
entries.summary: Contrast and movement attract attention: place signals where they stand out against the surroundings.
entries.detail: Use bright or contrasting materials against snow, rock, or vegetation. In open areas, create large shapes that are visible from a distance or from the air.
checklist: The signal contrasts with its surroundings
The signal is visible from a distance
decision_rules: If the signal blends in, move it or add contrast
If you hear or see searchers, prioritize being seen over creating more signals
prohibitions: Do not place signals where they are hidden by terrain
Do not use signals that could be mistaken for ordinary activity

entries.title: Communication discipline
entries.summary: When contact is established, communicate clearly and conserve power for further contact.
entries.detail: State your position, your situation, and what you need, then listen. Keep messages short and repeat key information.
checklist: Position is known and ready to state
decision_rules: If the connection is weak, repeat only the essential facts
If power is low, reduce transmission frequency
prohibitions: Do not turn off a device that has established contact
